bounds_cases.label: single_keypart_equality
bounds_cases.note: one keypart, low == high, both inclusive. normalize() has an explicit special case for exactly this shape at the end of the function - it returns an open-ended range rather than a closed one

bounds_cases.label: two_keypart_equality
bounds_cases.note: two equality keyparts - the equality prefix should absorb both

bounds_cases.label: equality_prefix_then_closed_range
bounds_cases.note: one equality then a bounded range - the prefix is collapsed and the range materializes on both sides

bounds_cases.label: equality_prefix_then_open_range
bounds_cases.note: same, but the range endpoints are exclusive - watch the open flags

bounds_cases.label: unbounded_high
bounds_cases.note: a range with no upper endpoint - normalize returns early with upper: None

bounds_cases.label: unbounded_low
bounds_cases.note: a range with no lower endpoint - the lower tuple stays short

bounds_cases.label: equality_prefix_then_unbounded_high
bounds_cases.note: equality prefix followed by a half-open range

bounds_cases.label: both_unbounded
bounds_cases.note: a keypart with no endpoints on either side

bounds_cases.label: infinity_datum
bounds_cases.note: a KeyDatum sentinel rather than an Endpoint sentinel - normalize's match arms do not treat KeyDatum::PosInfinity as a value, so this exits early

plan_cases.note: equality-only, single column
equality-only, composite - keypart order follows conjunct order, not name order
one inequality, no ORDER BY
two inequalities on different fields - one index plan per inequality field
two inequalities on the SAME field - one bounded range, not two plans
equality prefix plus a range on the next keypart
ORDER-FIRST with a single DESC key. Under indexeddb the index is ASC-only and the scan reverses; under full_support the keypart itself is DESC
ORDER-FIRST with a single DESC key. Under indexeddb the index is ASC-only and the scan reverses; under full_support the keypart itself is DESC
mixed-direction ORDER BY - the case the two configs disagree on. indexeddb keeps the longest same-direction prefix and spills the rest; full_support satisfies the whole ordering in the index
plan_cases.query: status = 'active' ORDER BY a ASC, b DESC

plan_cases.note: mixed-direction ORDER BY - the case the two configs disagree on. indexeddb keeps the longest same-direction prefix and spills the rest; full_support satisfies the whole ordering in the index
plan_cases.query: status = 'active' ORDER BY a ASC, b DESC

plan_cases.note: uniform DESC ORDER BY - indexeddb can serve it all by reversing the scan, so nothing spills even without DESC index support
plan_cases.query: status = 'active' ORDER BY a DESC, b DESC

plan_cases.note: uniform DESC ORDER BY - indexeddb can serve it all by reversing the scan, so nothing spills even without DESC index support
plan_cases.query: status = 'active' ORDER BY a DESC, b DESC

plan_cases.note: covered inequality: the ORDER BY field is the one with the range, so INEQ-FIRST is deliberately suppressed and only ORDER-FIRST is emitted
uncovered inequality: the ORDER BY field has no range, so both ORDER-FIRST and INEQ-FIRST are emitted
equality plus an uncovered inequality plus an unrelated ORDER BY
plan_cases.query: status = 'active' AND score > 5 ORDER BY name ASC

plan_cases.note: primary-key equality only - index generation is skipped and a table scan is returned directly
primary-key range only - short-circuits to a single table scan with primary key bounds
primary-key range plus primary-key ORDER BY - short-circuits, and the scan direction comes from the ORDER BY
primary-key ORDER BY alongside a non-primary predicate - the short-circuit does NOT apply because there is another meaningful predicate
contradictory range on one field - the bounds are empty, so EmptyScan, and no table-scan fallback is appended
OR breaks the conjunct chain: ConjunctFinder yields the whole OR as one opaque conjunct, so no index is usable and the whole predicate is residual
an OR nested inside an AND - the equality is still indexable, the OR stays in remaining_predicate
IS NULL is not an equality or a range, so it cannot drive an index
empty query - the parser yields Predicate::True, which is not indexable; expect a bare table scan
LIMIT is carried on the Selection but the planner ignores it - the plans must be identical to the bare equality case
a dotted path as the indexed column - watch whether sub_path is populated
